structure.heading: Financial Health Assessment and Quality of Earnings Conclusions
text_content: **Financial Health Assessment and Quality of Earnings Conclusions**
$68.1M as the starting point, with sensitivity to ±200–400 basis points in EBITDA margin to reflect integration and pricing risks and macro uncertainty.

Quality of earnings analysis reduces headline EBITDA: Normalized EBITDA is $61.3M after $6.8M of add-backs are removed. The $6.8M comprises items identified by finance as non-recurring, one-time transaction-related costs, and certain discretionary owner benefits; these were not sustainable in normal operations. Reconciliations to audited statements revealed timing differences in revenue recognition and a $2.1M working capital benefit in FY2024. We recommend using normalized EBITDA of $61.3M for covenant testing and base valuation, with stress scenarios modeling further 5–10% downside period.
$61.3M = 1.98x). This leverage profile provides headroom for integration but requires monitoring of covenant triggers and interest coverage under downside scenarios.

spec.subtitle: Ref: DD-3491584 | Date: 04 May 2026 | Prepared for: Apex Industrial Holdings Board

sections.heading: Executive Financial Overview
sections.body: Target company Meridian Process Systems, Inc. generated $128.4 million in revenue for FY2025, reflecting a 9.7% CAGR over the past three fiscal years. Adjusted EBITDA for FY2025 was $18.6 million (14.5% margin), compared to $15.2 million in FY2024, driven primarily by expanded service contracts in the Midwest region. Net working capital stands at $21.3 million, with inventory turns declining from 5.8x to 4.9x year-over-year due to supply chain buffering. Total funded debt is $42.7 million, resulting in a net leverage ratio of 2.3x EBITDA.

sections.heading: Quality of Earnings and Cash Flow
sections.body: Our review identified approximately $2.1 million in non-recurring expenses related to a facility consolidation completed in Q3 2025. Normalized free cash flow for FY2025 is estimated at $11.4 million after adjusting for one-time integration costs and deferred maintenance. Customer concentration risk is moderate, with the top three clients representing 37% of annual revenue; however, all major contracts extend beyond 24 months. Accounts receivable aging is stable, with 92% of balances under 60 days.

sections.heading: Legal and Regulatory Exposure
sections.body: Meridian is currently party to two ongoing disputes: a $1.8 million supplier indemnification claim and an employment misclassification lawsuit filed in February 2026. External counsel has assessed the likelihood of material loss as low to moderate, with an estimated exposure range of $0.6–$1.2 million after insurance recoveries. Environmental compliance reviews at the Ohio and Texas facilities identified minor reporting lapses but no hazardous violations. No change-of-control clauses were triggered in key customer agreements upon review.

sections.heading: Operational Risks and Integration Considerations
sections.body: Operationally, the company relies on a single-source manufacturer for specialized control valves representing 22% of cost of goods sold, posing supply continuity risk. ERP systems are partially customized and will require integration investment estimated at $1.5–$2.0 million to align with Apex’s SAP platform. Workforce turnover has declined to 11% annually following implementation of retention bonuses, though key engineering roles remain concentrated in two senior employees. Facility utilization averages 74%, leaving moderate headroom for volume growth without significant capex.

sections.heading: Synergy Potential and Valuation Range
sections.body: Revenue synergies are projected at $6–8 million annually by cross-selling Meridian’s maintenance services into Apex’s existing petrochemical client base. Cost synergies of approximately $3.2 million per year are expected from procurement consolidation and elimination of duplicative corporate overhead. Applying a blended 7.0x–8.0x normalized EBITDA multiple to adjusted EBITDA of $20.7 million yields an enterprise valuation range of $145–$166 million. After deducting net debt, the implied equity value range is $102–$123 million, which we consider defensible subject to final confirmatory diligence.

structure.full_text:
Due Diligence Summary – Financial, Legal, and Operational Assessment
Ref: DD-3491584 | Date: 04 May 2026 | Prepared for: Apex Industrial Holdings Board

Section Executive Financial Overview
Target company Meridian Process Systems, Inc. generated $128.4 million in revenue for FY2025, reflecting a 9.7% CAGR over the past three fiscal years. Adjusted EBITDA for FY2025 was $18.6 million (14.5% margin), compared to $15.2 million in FY2024, driven primarily by expanded service contracts in the Midwest region. Net working capital stands at $21.3 million, with inventory turns declining from 5.8x to 4.9x year-over-year due to supply chain buffering. Total funded debt is $42.7 million, resulting in a net leverage ratio of 2.3x EBITDA.

Section Quality of Earnings and Cash Flow
Our review identified approximately $2.1 million in non-recurring expenses related to a facility consolidation completed in Q3 2025. Normalized free cash flow for FY2025 is estimated at $11.4 million after adjusting for one-time integration costs and deferred maintenance. Customer concentration risk is moderate, with the top three clients representing 37% of annual revenue; however, all major contracts extend beyond 24 months. Accounts receivable aging is stable, with 92% of balances under 60 days.

Section Legal and Regulatory Exposure
Meridian is currently party to two ongoing disputes: a $1.8 million supplier indemnification claim and an employment misclassification lawsuit filed in February 2026. External counsel has assessed the likelihood of material loss as low to moderate, with an estimated exposure range of $0.6–$1.2 million after insurance recoveries. Environmental compliance reviews at the Ohio and Texas facilities identified minor reporting lapses but no hazardous violations. No change-of-control clauses were triggered in key customer agreements upon review.

Section Operational Risks and Integration Considerations
Operationally, the company relies on a single-source manufacturer for specialized control valves representing 22% of cost of goods sold, posing supply continuity risk. ERP systems are partially customized and will require integration investment estimated at $1.5–$2.0 million to align with Apex’s SAP platform. Workforce turnover has declined to 11% annually following implementation of retention bonuses, though key engineering roles remain concentrated in two senior employees. Facility utilization averages 74%, leaving moderate headroom for volume growth without significant capex.

Section Synergy Potential and Valuation Range
Revenue synergies are projected at $6–8 million annually by cross-selling Meridian’s maintenance services into Apex’s existing petrochemical client base. Cost synergies of approximately $3.2 million per year are expected from procurement consolidation and elimination of duplicative corporate overhead. Applying a blended 7.0x–8.0x normalized EBITDA multiple to adjusted EBITDA of $20.7 million yields an enterprise valuation range of $145–$166 million. After deducting net debt, the implied equity value range is $102–$123 million, which we consider defensible subject to final confirmatory diligence.

Confidential — For Board Review Only | Page 1 of 2

structure.heading: Legal Exposure, Operational Risk Profile, Synergy Case, and Valuation Range Recommendation
text_content: **Legal Exposure, Operational Risk Profile, Synergy Case, and Valuation Range Recommendation**

TargetCo faces a material legal exposure from Apex Systems v. TargetCo, filed 2024-11-18, which seeks $24.0M in damages. Legal counsel advises monitoring for developments that could require a contingent liability accrual under GAAP if loss becomes probable and estimable; absent such determination we recommend setting aside a litigation reserve and confirming insurance limits and indemnities. Anticipated timelines to resolution range 12–36 months; settlement scenarios between $0.5M and $18.0M should be modeled in cash-flow sensitivities to assess downside to enterprise value.

Operational risk concentrates on integration complexity, supplier single‑source exposures, IT and ERP migration, and retention of key personnel, each presenting measurable execution risk. We note potential working capital volatility during integration and recommend: 1. immediate supplier contract reviews; 2. targeted key‑employee retention packages; and 3. an ERP cutover contingency plan. Compliance and data‑privacy controls require a pre-close gap assessment. Together these mitigations reduce probability of disruption and preserve projected cash flows pending detailed post‑close operational service levels.

We estimate annual run‑rate synergies of $22.5M by Year 3, comprised of $14.0M from procurement and $8.5M from SG&A consolidation. Assumptions include a 70–85% capture rate and implementation costs front‑loaded in Year 1–2; sensitivity analysis should reflect slower capture and one‑time integration charges. Based on these projections and $61.3M Normalized EBITDA, our recommended enterprise value range is $490M–$610M, implying multiples of 8.0x–10.0x. We recommend staged payments, escrow, and earnouts where appropriate post-close.
